Related PR for the TUI session picker side: #26432.

That PR fixes the root-session dilution in the TUI dialog by querying root sessions directly for `/sessions` while leaving the shared session bootstrap unchanged for child-session navigation.

It does not claim to fix the separate MCP/session-tool source-of-truth mismatch reported here (`session_list`/`session_read` behavior). I am calling that out so the two layers do not get conflated.

Authorship disclosure: prepared with AI assistance.

Context on #23276 overlap:

This is intentionally close to #23276's narrow-dialog approach, but it adds two differences that should help avoid the earlier stale/template/design problems:

1. The default dialog query does not include the bootstrap 30-day `start` filter. It asks for the latest 100 root sessions directly, which better matches the CLI root-session behavior and addresses reports where older root sessions are hidden.
2. The root-query construction is covered by `test/cli/tui/dialog-session-list.test.ts`, so the dialog-specific scope is explicit and protected.

It still keeps the important design constraint from the #24383 discussion: the shared `sync.data.session` bootstrap remains mixed and unchanged for parent/child navigation.

> ## Stitch MCP - Bug Report: "Failed to get tools"
> ### Problem
> When configuring Google Stitch as a remote MCP server in opencode, the error "stitch Failed to get tools" appears and Stitch tools are not loaded.
> 
> ### Environment
> * opencode version: 1.14.33
> * OS: macOS
> * Stitch MCP endpoint: https://stitch.googleapis.com/mcp
> 
> ### Configuration
> {
>   "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
>   "mcp": {
>     "stitch": {
>       "type": "remote",
>       "url": "https://stitch.googleapis.com/mcp",
>       "enabled": true,
>       "headers": {
>         "X-Goog-Api-Key": "<API_KEY>"
>       }
>     }
>   }
> }
> ### What works
> * Direct curl to Stitch endpoint with POST returns tools correctly
> * The Stitch API responds correctly (405 on GET, 200 on POST with tools)
> 
> ### What doesn't work
> * opencode fails to load Stitch MCP tools despite API key being valid, config correct, and API responding properly to direct requests
> 
> ### Tested variations
> 1. Config with only Stitch MCP (no other providers/MCP servers) → Same error
> 2. Other remote MCP servers work fine with similar configuration
> 3. API key works via curl but not via opencode
> 
> ### Conclusion
> Bug in how opencode 1.14.33 handles the `X-Goog-Api-Key` header for remote MCP servers, or how it parses the response from Google's Stitch MCP endpoint.
> 
> ### Related Issues
> * [Agents and Commands are not shown #8868](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/8868) - Similar MCP remote server issues
> 
> ### Expected behavior
> Stitch MCP tools should be available in opencode when configured correctly.

Hitting this on the **official prebuilt release binary** (v1.14.41, Linux x64),
which suggests this isn't just a local dev / Bun cache issue - the duplicate is shipped in the release.

## Root cause

The release tarball includes **two copies** of `@opentui/solid` in `node_modules`:

node_modules/@opentui/solid                              → v0.2.2  (used by opencode)
node_modules/opentui-spinner/node_modules/@opentui/solid → v0.1.105 (used by opentui-spinner)

`opentui-spinner` declares `@opentui/solid: ^0.1.49` as a peer dependency, while the workspace catalog pins `@opentui/solid` to `0.2.2`. Since
`0.2.2` doesn't satisfy `^0.1.49`, Bun installs a separate copy under `opentui-spinner/node_modules/`.

`opentui-spinner/dist/solid.mjs` calls `extend({ spinner: ... })`, but that `extend` resolves to the **v0.1.105** instance and registers the
component on its own `componentCatalogue`. The TUI itself uses **v0.2.2**, whose catalogue never receives the registration. When `<spinner>` is
rendered, the v0.2.2 reconciler throws `Unknown component type: spinner`.

I verified this by inspecting strings in the compiled binary — both `extend({ spinner: ... })` calls are present, but they target different
module instances. This also explains why `rm -rf node_modules && bun install && bun run build --single` *sometimes* works for people: depending
on the resolver state, Bun occasionally hoists a single copy and the bug disappears, but it isn't deterministic.

## Verified fix

Adding the following to the **root** `package.json` `overrides`, then `bun install --force` and rebuilding, eliminates the duplicate and fixes
the crash:

```json
"overrides": {
"@opentui/solid": "0.2.2",
"@opentui/core": "0.2.2"
}

After this, node_modules/opentui-spinner/node_modules/@opentui/ no longer exists, and the rebuilt binary renders the spinner correctly. Confirmed
locally on Linux x64 with v1.14.41.

Suggested upstream fixes

1. Add the override above to this repo so prebuilt releases never ship the duplicate, or
2. Bump opentui-spinner to widen its peer dep range (e.g. ^0.1.49 || ^0.2.0) - the extend() API used by opentui-spinner/dist/solid.mjs is identical between v0.1.x and v0.2.2, so no code change in the spinner itself should be needed.

I can confirm this still reproduces on Windows with OpenCode `1.14.41`.

Environment:

- OS: Windows 11
- OpenCode: `opencode-ai 1.14.41`
- Mode: `opencode serve` / `opencode web`
- Browser access through localhost

Local evidence from the same machine:

```text
project.worktree = C:\Users\zhangqianfeng\playground
session.directory = C:\Users\zhangqianfeng\playground
root sessions for that directory = 9
```

The server API behaves differently only based on slash style:

```text
GET /session?directory=C%3A%5CUsers%5Czhangqianfeng%5Cplayground&roots=true&limit=55
=> returns 9 sessions

GET /session?directory=C%3A%2FUsers%2Fzhangqianfeng%2Fplayground&roots=true&limit=55
=> returns 0 sessions
```

So the data is present and the issue is still an exact-match path separator mismatch.

One important detail: PR #23862 normalizes client-side map/cache keys and says it does not change the raw directory value passed to API calls. That may not fully fix this direct API failure, because `/session?directory=C:/Users/...` still misses rows stored as `C:\Users\...`.

A robust fix may also be needed server-side in session listing, for example by accepting equivalent Windows directory variants when filtering `SessionTable.directory`:

```ts
function windowsDirectoryVariants(directory: string) {
  if (!/^[a-zA-Z]:[\\/]/.test(directory) && !directory.startsWith("\\\\") && !directory.startsWith("//")) {
    return [directory]
  }
  return Array.from(new Set([directory, directory.replaceAll("/", "\\"), directory.replaceAll("\\", "/")]))
}

function directoryCondition(directory: string) {
  const variants = windowsDirectoryVariants(directory)
  if (variants.length === 1) return eq(SessionTable.directory, directory)
  return or(...variants.map((item) => eq(SessionTable.directory, item)))!
}
```

Then use that condition anywhere session listing currently does:

```ts
eq(SessionTable.directory, input.directory)
```

Affected places I found:

- `packages/opencode/src/session/session.ts`
- `packages/opencode/src/v2/session.ts`

Temporary workaround that confirms the diagnosis: a local proxy that rewrites only query/header directory values from `C:/Users/...` to `C:\Users\...` makes the Web UI show the full session list again.

Dropping per discussion — the race this guards against doesn't manifest in the new `socket.runRaw` ordering, the test is expensive (~20s/CI), and it leaks `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD`/`USERNAME` into subsequent tests. Replacing with a 2-line comment in the prod handler explaining why no buffer is needed.
